newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S COSATU AGAINST ACCELERATED TARIFF CUTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S COSATU AGAINST ACCELERATED TARIFF CUTS.

text.p: South Africa's trade liberalisation programme should be held back until measures aimed at boosting the country's industry were put in place, the country's largest union federation said on Tuesday.

Addressing a public hearing on trade and industry policy in Pretoria, Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) representative Herbert Mkhize said tariff reduction had to be preceded by supply-side measures aimed at improving the performance and competitiveness of South African industry.
"The important issue is that we cannot blindly commit to tariff reduction without locating the process in a way that benefits South Africans," Mkhize said.
"There should be a review of the current trade liberalisation programme so that tariff policy is deployed as an overall tool of industrial and development policy," he added.

Mkhize said supply-side measures included a national restructuring fund to help companies finance the introduction of new technology and work organisation; a four percent levy on companies' payrolls to finance the retraining of workers; and the improvement of competition legislation.
In its macro-economic strategy unveiled on June 14, the South African government said the rand's depreciation against the dollar this year would allow the country to speed up tariff cuts.
Average tariffs as a percentage of imports are expected to fall from 10 percent this year to eight percent by the year 2000.
Cosatu said the rand's recent fall should be viewed as an opportunity to help local industry compete against imports.
The rand has lost about 25 percent of its value against the dollar since February 15 this year.

Mkhize said where significant job losses were to result from tariff reduction, there should be a clear commitment from government that it would not reduce tariffs faster than was required in terms of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.
